description: Experience the quintessential taste of the American coast with this classic New England Clam Chowder. This hearty soup features tender clams, crispy bacon, and diced potatoes in a rich, creamy broth. Perfect for a chilly evening, it is a comforting and satisfying meal.

instructions.title: Cook Bacon
instructions.text: In a large Dutch oven or heavy pot, cook diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving about 2 tablespoons of bacon fat in the pot.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Add diced onion and celery to the pot with bacon fat. Cook over medium heat until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Do not brown.

instructions.title: Thicken Base
instructions.text: Sprinkle flour over the cooked vegetables and stir for 1 minute to create a roux. Gradually whisk in the reserved clam juice (from canned clams) and the bottled clam juice until smooth, ensuring no lumps.

instructions.title: Simmer Potatoes
instructions.text: Add diced potatoes to the pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Add Dairy and Clams
instructions.text: Pour in the heavy cream and whole milk. Add the drained chopped clams to the pot. Stir gently and heat through, making sure the chowder does not boil after adding dairy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Ladle the hot New England Clam Chowder into bowls. Garnish each serving with the reserved crispy bacon and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with oyster crackers.

tips: For extra flavor, consider adding a dash of dry sherry or a pinch of dried thyme to the chowder along with the dairy.
Avoid boiling the chowder once dairy is added, as high heat can cause the cream to curdle. Gently simmer over low heat until heated through.
Store leftover chowder in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave.
